summary: TM-16's 'extend the rebuild to releases whose agent came from an earlier commit' (ADR-0141, proposed). CI and tooling only. The release-provenance job rebuild-and-attest keeps its permissions and its rule (attest only bytes a rebuild reproduces). Changes: checkout with fetch-depth 0 (earlier tags); a second checkout (same pinned action, persist-credentials false, sparse) of the workflow's own commit for tools/security/rebuild_agent.sh, so a manual run for an older tag runs the reviewed script, not the tag's; a step that finds the oldest release whose assets include skirnir-agent-<version>-linux-amd64 via gh (tag names filtered to v<digits>.<digits>.<digits>; the version comes from the published file name already validated to digits and dots); the rebuild step runs the script with HEAD and that tag. The script: set -euo pipefail, refuses a missing binary and a non-numeric version, skips refs that are not commits, builds from git archive of the ref (no working tree), compares only the two binaries (SBOMs next to them ignored, which also fixes manual re-runs where SBOMs were already attached), keeps the binaries only for the reproducing ref and clears them otherwise. Inputs reaching the shell: the release tag (env, argument only, as before), tag names from the repository's own releases (filtered), asset names (compared, not executed). The attestation still names the workflow run at the release tag; the step summary records which ref reproduced the bytes (documented consequence).

findings.evidence: Release provenance run for v0.35.1 (2026-11-16) failed: the Windows binary of agent 0.35.1, published unchanged from v0.34.1, was not reproduced from the v0.35.1 tag after a golang.org/x/sys bump in agent/; the release has no attestation or SBOMs. Pre-existing.
findings.resolution: rebuild from the release that first published the version when the tag does not reproduce it; reproduced locally (tag alone fails as in CI, tag then origin succeeds). A manual run for v0.35.1 after the merge would attest it (needs the maintainer's go-ahead: it writes to a published release).

tests.command: local reproduction: agent 0.35.1 built from v0.35.0's agent/ as 'published'; rebuild_agent.sh with v0.35.1, then with v0.35.1 v0.35.0
tests.evidence: tag alone: Windows DIFFERENT, Linux identical, exit 1, nothing left in out (as the CI run); tag then v0.35.0: both identical, 'REBUILT FROM v0.35.0', exit 0; an SBOM file next to the binaries ignored; refused: missing binary (exit 2), version '0.35.1;x' (exit 2), unknown ref skipped then exit 1.

tests.command: origin search (read-only gh release list/view against the real releases)
tests.evidence: agent 0.35.1 -> v0.34.1 (agent/ identical to v0.35.0's), agent 0.35.2 -> v0.36.0.

tests.command: yaml parse of release-provenance.yml; python test/check_pinned_references.py; selftest_pinned_references; bash -n tools/security/rebuild_agent.sh
tests.evidence: steps in order; 0 pin findings; 0 failures; syntax ok.

tests.command: every python test/... and tools/... command of all workflows in .github/workflows/, except run_tests.py and check_public_changes; plus ruff check .

limitations: The workflow itself runs only on a published release or a manual run; the local test used the local Go toolchain, not the one recorded in the published binaries, so it proves the logic, not the real hashes.
The attestation's workflow reference is the release tag even when the bytes were rebuilt from an earlier release.
